summary: Closure review of a preregistered, emulation‑grounded paired experiment comparing a GVR (generate–validate–repair) pipeline to an LLM‑only baseline. The archived execution and analysis artifacts are complete and internally consistent but the revised manuscript still contains presentation and citation defects that prevent finalisation. The core scientific record (degenerate paired outcome: n=240 pairs, all pairs safe under both arms; paired difference = 0.00; 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0) is artifact‑grounded and sound; required editorial fixes remain.
critical_issues: Main manuscript text, figures, captions, and tables include run‑internal file paths and multiple full SHA‑256 digests (e.g., execution/*.jsonl, analysis/*.csv and explicit SHA‑256 strings). The track requires that only the single mandatory master_prompt locator+SHA appear in the Disclosure Statement; other low‑level provenance must remain only in the archived execution bundle and must not be reprinted in ordinary prose.

The Disclosure Statement duplicates execution accounting, per‑call provenance, and multiple per‑file hashes instead of being a concise paragraph limited to the required elements (declared model(s) and identifiers, adapter/validator ids, preregistration id+SHA, the single immutable master_prompt locator+SHA, a concise autonomy/human boundary, and a high‑level pointer to the archived execution manifest).

References and in‑text citation formatting are not in conventional IEEE numbered bibliography form throughout; some bibliography entries are identifier‑only (arXiv/DOI/URL strings) or lack full IEEE bibliographic metadata. Several in‑text citation placements should be verified to ensure the cited record actually supports the nearby claim.
required_revisions: Remove all run‑internal file paths and full SHA‑256 digests from main manuscript prose, figures, captions, tables, and Results/Methods narrative. Preserve these detailed provenance artifacts only in the archived execution bundle. Keep exactly one master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 and place it only inside the Disclosure Statement.

Condense the Disclosure Statement to a short, self‑contained paragraph that lists only: declared model(s) and identifiers (e.g., "gpt‑5‑mini"), adapter/orchestration family and validator identifier (hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic_netops_validator_v5), preregistration id and SHA‑256, the single immutable master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 (required), a concise human/autonomy boundary statement, and a brief pointer to the archived execution manifest (no per‑file paths or hashes). Remove duplicated execution logs, per‑call trace paths, and per‑file hashes from the Disclosure Statement.

Replace all identifier‑only or nonstandard Reference entries with full IEEE‑style bibliographic entries using the available verified metadata in terminal_bibliographic_records. Use numbered IEEE in‑text citation markers and ensure each numbered citation actually supports the proximate scholarly claim; adjust claim wording or citation placement where the record does not directly support the assertion.
optional_revisions: Optionally add a single short qualifier in the Abstract (one sentence) stating up front that the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics made the primary paired estimand uninformative in this run (to set reader expectation early).

Move long example JSON snippets, validator‑trace excerpts, and other machine‑readable artifact excerpts out of the main prose; either omit them or reference them by archive pointer. If a compact appendix within the five pages is retained, ensure it does not reprint full hashes or internal paths.

Optionally include a short high‑level checklist in Methods mapping preregistered analysis items to archived artifact filenames (high‑level pointers only, without hashes) to aid traceability for readers.
